findings.title: .small-action button { float: right } is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: This change makes `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at the top of the rule), but the nested `button { float: right; }` at line 309 was left unchanged. Floats on flex items are ignored by the flexbox spec, so the float has no effect. Previously the button (e.g. the small-action buttons in the topic stream) was pushed to the far right edge of the row; now it will sit immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text with default spacing, since no `margin-left: auto` was added to replace the float. The trailing `clear: both` on `.small-action` (line 312) is likewise dead. The button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the container needs `justify-content: space-between`) to restore right-edge alignment.

findings.title: -ms-align-items is not a real vendor-prefixed property
findings.body: The new `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. No browser has ever implemented a property with that name; Microsoft's flexbox prefixes are `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the line above) and, for the modern syntax, the unprefixed `align-items` (also already emitted). This declaration is always invalid and silently dropped, adding dead code to the generated stylesheet for every flex-aligned rule. It should be removed.

findings.title: margin-left: auto on .panel does not right-align in the legacy flexbox implementations the mixins target
findings.body: The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits the 2009 syntax (`display: -webkit-box`, `display: -moz-box`) and the IE10 syntax (`display: -ms-flexbox`), but the right-alignment of the header panel relies solely on `margin-left: auto` on `.panel`. Auto-margin packing in flex containers is a feature of the final flexbox spec: IE10's `-ms-flexbox` implementation notoriously ignores auto margins for alignment, and the 2009 `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` spec provides `box-pack` instead. So in exactly the older browsers these prefixes were added for, the search/hamburger/user panel will not be pushed to the right edge and will sit next to the site title, breaking the header layout. Either add a `box-pack: end`-based fallback or accept dropping the ancient-prefix output.
